previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted for acute shortness of breath and severe hypertension, with initial presentation of pulmonary edema. She had recently undergone dialysis but developed fluid overload, leading to flash pulmonary edema. She was stabilized with blood pressure management and a session of hemodialysis, after which her respiratory symptoms resolved. Her INR was found to be supratherapeutic at 4.1, prompting a two-day hold on warfarin, with plans to restart post-discharge. She remained hemodynamically stable, with no evidence of infection or acute coronary syndrome. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart anticoagulation, monitor INR, adhere to fluid and sodium restrictions, and follow up with her specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo woman with h/o CHF, hyperlipidemia, PVD, DM2 
and CKD who presented s/p dialysis with chest pain and 
hypotension. 
.  
#. Coronary Artery Disease:  The patient had an episode of chest 
pain prior to dialysis on the day of admission.  The pain was 
concerning for unstable angina or NSTEMI, given the patient's 
cardiac history and ECG changes, but it was relieved with 
dialysis and she did not have any associated symptoms.  In 
addition, her cardiac markers were negative on this admission.  
Given the patient's recent cardiac catheterization ___ TTE 
(___), it was decided that she has a low probability for lesion 
on stress test.  Thus, the patient was continued on her 
outpatient dose of Metoprolol, Valsartan, Aspirin, Lisinopril, 
and Atorvastatin.  She was monitored on telemetry and did not 
have any further episodes of chest pain during this admission. 
.  
#. Congestive Heart Failure:  The patient has a history of CHF 
with outflow tract obstruction and EF > 75% on ECHO (___).  The 
patient has a very delicate fluid balance and is dependant on HD 
for diuresis.  She appeared euvolemic on physical exam during 
this admission.  She was continued on her home dose of 
Lisinopril and Valsartan, and she received hemodialysis on the 
day after admission.   
.  
#. Atrial Fibrillation:  The patient has a history of PAFib.  
She is currently on Amiodarone for rhythm control and Coumadin 
for anticoagulation.  She has apparently been increasingly in 
AFib over the past few months and is not responding to 
Amiodarone. Electrophysiology was consulted on this admission, 
and it was recommended to increase her dose of Amiodarone to 600 
mg for one week and then continue at a higher dose of 400 mg 
daily thereafter.  The patient was started on this new regimen, 
and her Warfarin was decreased to 2 mg daily.  She will follow 
up with her outpatient cardiologist regarding this issue in 
___.
.
#. Type 2 Diabetes:  The patient has a history of DM2.  She is 
currently on Insulin NPH at home. She was continued on her home 
dose of Insulin and she was started on an insulin sliding scale 
on this admission with finger sticks every four hours.  She did 
not have any acute events during this admission.
.  
#. ESRD on HD:  The patient had one hour of HD on the day of 
admission.  She was thus dialyzed on the second day of admission 
and did not experience any episodes of hypotension.  The patient 
was followed by the nephrology team during this admission, and 
she did not have any acute events.  
.  
#. L eye blindness:  The patient has a history of blindness in 
her Left eye.  On admission, the patient's left eye was very 
indurated on physical exam, and she states that she had an 
episode of eye pain the day prior to admission.  She was started 
on her home eye drops, and her eye appeared markedly improved on 
discharge.
.
#. GERD:  The patient has a history of GERD.  She is currently 
on Ranitidine and Pantoprazole at home.  She was continued on 
these home medications, and she did not have any acute events 
during this hospital stay.
